reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a creator-run makeup giveaway offering specified gift cards and makeup products, with winners selected through a random drawing. Participation involves subscribing, commenting, following the creator's Instagram account, and optionally sharing for an extra entry, which is described as ordinary audience engagement rather than a financial or credential transaction. The sampled frames show makeup-related items referenced by the giveaway, while prize delivery and account authenticity remain unresolved.

citations.quote: Here are the rules to enter this makeup giveaway: Rule #1: Subscribe to my channel. Rule #2: Comment down below which item you would like to win. Rule #3: Follow me on Instagram

The 1st person that I pick will win the Sephora $20 gift card. -The 2nd person that I pick will win the Ulta $20 gift card. -The 3rd person that I pick will win the Jeffree Star x Morphe Eye Brush Collection. -The 4th person that I pick will win the Amrezy Palette.
But if you want an extra entry, just share this video on your Instagram or your Facebook. And you'll get an extra entry.
I will be doing a random drawing and this is how winners will be chosen for each item

opening.argument: This is a solicitation built around a low-barrier reward: the video offers four valuable-seeming prizes, but access is tied to a sequence of audience actions rather than a simple gift. Entry requires subscribing, commenting, and following an Instagram account, while sharing creates an additional advantage. The promised items are explicitly connected to those conditions, including two gift cards and branded makeup products. That reward-for-engagement structure is the operative offer, so the presentation can reasonably be treated as an acquisition scheme even though no cash deposit is requested.

citations.quote: Here are the rules to enter this makeup giveaway: Rule #1: Subscribe to my channel. Rule #2: Comment down below which item you would like to win. Rule #3: Follow me on Instagram
But if you want an extra entry, just share this video on your Instagram or your Facebook. And you'll get an extra entry.
The 1st person that I pick will win the Sephora $20 gift card. -The 2nd person that I pick will win the Ulta $20 gift card.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the actions ordinary engagement does not remove the linkage: the rules make subscribing, commenting, and following conditions of entry, and sharing increases a participant's chances. A random drawing describes selection, but it does not negate that viewers are being induced to perform several actions for a promised reward. The defense also concedes that prize delivery and account authenticity remain unresolved, leaving the central promise unverified.

citations.quote: Rule #1: Subscribe to my channel. Rule #2: Comment down below which item you would like to win. Rule #3: Follow me on Instagram
And you'll get an extra entry.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The defense would answer that an entry condition is not a claim that every participant receives a reward: the description says the creator will conduct a random drawing, and it assigns prizes to the first through fourth selected people. The actions requested are channel and social-media engagement, not payment or account credentials. The quotes therefore establish a promotional contest with uncertain eligibility and outcome, not a guaranteed asset acquisition.

citations.quote: I will be doing a random drawing and this is how winners will be chosen for each item
The 4th person that I pick will win the Amrezy Palette.

opening.argument: Several warning signals appear together: the offer presents gift cards and branded products as readily obtainable, imposes a fixed start and end window, directs viewers to an external Instagram account for the winner announcement, and gives an extra entry for social sharing. The combination creates urgency and expands the promoter's reach while requiring viewers to move between platforms and perform more than one engagement step. The evidence does not establish that the prizes will be delivered, so the unusually easy reward claim should be treated cautiously rather than presumed legitimate.

citations.quote: Giveaway will start today, January 21st and end February 9th.
I will announce the winner on February 9th on my Instagram Story: michaelsuarezz_
But if you want an extra entry, just share this video on your Instagram or your Facebook.
The 1st person that I pick will win the Sephora $20 gift card.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on the absence of a payment request, but the concern here is the cluster of signals: a time-limited reward, off-platform announcement, multiple required actions, and an extra-entry incentive. A genuine random-drawing statement does not verify fulfillment or explain why viewers should trust the external account. Showing products also proves only that products were displayed, not that winners will receive them.

citations.quote: I will announce the winner on February 9th on my Instagram Story: michaelsuarezz_
And you'll get an extra entry.
I will be doing a random drawing

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The defense would respond that these are ordinary contest mechanics, not proof of deception. The stated dates define the contest period, the Instagram story is simply where the winner will be announced, and the extra entry is explicitly optional. Most importantly, the selection method is identified as random, and the evidence contains no request for money, credentials, or a claim of guaranteed winnings.

citations.quote: Giveaway will start today, January 21st and end February 9th.
I will be doing a random drawing and this is how winners will be chosen for each item
But if you want an extra entry

opening.argument: The ordinary-giveaway framing should not obscure the video's promotional function. The title foregrounds free branded makeup and gift cards, the speaker displays the named products, and the rules direct viewers toward subscribing and following a particular Instagram identity. The on-screen rule specifically identifies that Instagram account, while the closing frame repeats the account branding. Taken together, the content is designed to steer viewers into the creator's social channels in exchange for a chance at advertised goods. That audience-acquisition pathway is consistent with a scam-like reward solicitation even without a separate purchase page.

citations.quote: MAKEUP GIVEAWAY | AMREZY PALETTE | JEFFREE STAR X MORPHE | ULTA GIFT CARD | SEPHORA GIFT CARD | FREE
Rule #3: Follow me on Instagram, I will announce the winner on February 9th on my Instagram Story: michaelsuarezz_

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense labels this ordinary promotion, but that is precisely the functional issue: the prize imagery and free-offer framing make the requested social actions more attractive. The displayed products do not establish ownership, inventory, or delivery, while the on-screen rule explicitly routes viewers to a named Instagram account. Calling it a giveaway describes the packaging, not whether the promised reward pathway is reliable.

citations.quote: Rule #3: Follow me on Instagram

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The defense would answer that promotional intent is not inherently deceptive. The title accurately identifies the makeup giveaway and its listed prizes, while the rules explain the participation steps and say winners will be selected by random drawing. The Instagram follow is disclosed as a rule rather than concealed, and product display supports the subject of the promotion without proving a fraudulent claim.
